title: phil-d-skills host file
description: One repo's answers to the questions the suite's skills ask. Lives at .agents/host.json in the repo root and is found by walking up from cwd. A slot carrying a value is the answer; a slot set to null says the repo has none of that thing, and the skill skips the step; an absent slot means nobody answered, and the skill runs its compatibility fallback.

template.description: Which host/templates/ file this was filled from. Recorded so a suite update can tell what a repo started from.

dev.description: Running the app. Read by verify-ui, decision-request, wrap-gate, new-screen, add-primitive and receive-prototype.

cwd.description: Directory the dev command runs in, relative to the repo root. Null or absent means the repo root.

start.description: Shell command that starts the app for review, run from dev.cwd. Null means the repo has no runnable app, and every skill that would look at a screen says so instead.

url.description: Base URL the started app is expected to bind. Every quoted link hangs off it, and the port the server ACTUALLY bound overrides it — a dev server walks up from its default whenever another holds the port.

platform.description: Which harness can see the app. `web` means a browser and a URL; `native` means a simulator and a screenshot, so a measured number is reported as looked at rather than measured.

checks.description: The typecheck, lint, test and format commands with the count each one is allowed to return. Read by wrap-gate/scripts/check-baseline.mjs, which also writes baselines back here under --record. Null means the repo has no automated checks.

cwd.description: Directory every check runs in, relative to the repo root. A check's own `cwd` overrides it.

guard.description: The repo's own prose or convention guard, where it has one beyond the four below. check-baseline runs it like any other check; write-doc and freeze-memory read its `cmd` to run it deliberately.

git.description: Branches and who merges. Read by open-pr, start-engagement and ask-issue-status.

trunk.description: Branch a finished piece of work is raised against by default.

release.description: Branch the trunk is caught up to, where the repo separates the two. Null means the trunk is also the release branch, and open-pr's § Variants does not run.

engagementBranch.description: Branch one client engagement's work lives on, where the repo carries per-engagement branches. Null means every branch is the same kind.

doc.description: Repo file holding the branch table, the pull-request templates and who merges. Cited rather than quoted.

docs.description: Where written rules live. Read by write-doc, new-screen, record-design, paper and ask-issue-status.

root.description: Folder holding the repo's docs. Null means the repo keeps no docs folder, and a doc is written where the reader who needs it will be.

glossary.description: File defining the repo's internal terms. A term with no entry gets one before its first use elsewhere.

gotchas.description: Index file routing to the repo's lessons-learned rules. Read before any interface work and written to when a correction produces a mechanism.

local.description: Folder for notes true on one branch only, which the trunk never takes. Null means every note is repo-wide.

retired.description: Folder holding retirement records — what is gone and why. Dated language is legal there and nowhere else.

index.description: File carrying the read-when index a planning agent reads first, usually AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. A doc added without a line here is a doc nobody finds.

records.description: The product record and the design records. Read by record-design, audit-design, ingest-theme, paper, start-engagement and receive-prototype.

product.description: File stating what the product is, who it serves and what its copy standard is. audit-design quotes its six criteria from here.

productTemplate.description: Stub the product record is filled from. Absent means start-engagement uses its own bundled template.

design.description: Every design record in the repo, most general first. Each entry names one surface and the file recording the system that surface landed.

surface.description: What the record covers, in the words the repo uses for it.

path.description: The record file, relative to the repo root.

sidecar.description: Machine-readable mirror of the record's rules, where a tool keeps one. Written LAST, because a staleness check compares modification times.

designDoc.description: File stating the canonical headings, their order and any length cap a design record owes. Absent means record-design uses its own bundled format.

driftWatch.description: Command reporting which design records have fallen behind the code. Null means drift is noticed by reading.

memory.description: One engagement's project notes. Read by write-doc, freeze-memory and start-engagement.

root.description: Folder holding the project notes. Null means the repo keeps none, and freeze-memory exits in one line.

archive.description: Folder a retired note moves to, carrying a pointer at whatever replaced it.

doc.description: File defining the note statuses and how each one is edited. Absent means freeze-memory uses its own bundled four.

gloss.description: Source file holding the one-line gloss per note that a listing renders. A note with no gloss lists blank.

connectors.description: Note recording which external services this engagement's material comes from, and which space or project inside each.

issues.description: The tracker and the per-surface issue ladder. Read by ask-issue-status, open-pr, new-surface and start-engagement.

tracker.description: Which issue tracker the repo's work answers to, named as the agent would reach it. Null means work is tracked outside any tool a skill can read.

ladder.description: Source file declaring which issues each surface's screens answer to, and each one's status. Null means the repo tracks status somewhere a skill does not write, and ask-issue-status exits in one line.

doc.description: File stating the rung shape, the status words and how a surface declares its issues.

ask.description: Command that prints the rungs to put to the designer. Absent means read the ladder file directly.

retired.description: True where the branch dropped the ladder on purpose. ask-issue-status then says so once and never asks again.

verify.description: Proving a rendered value rather than assuming it. Read by verify-ui, wrap-gate, decision-request, record-design and add-primitive.

mcp.description: Which browser-driving tool the repo uses to LOOK at a screen. Null means nothing can drive the app, and every number is reported as looked at rather than measured.

probes.description: Folder holding the scripts that MEASURE the rendered page. Null means no number can be asserted, and a write-up says which values went unmeasured.

doc.description: File holding the repo's probe table and the traps each probe has already paid for. Absent means verify-ui uses its own bundled measuring rules.

agent.description: Sub-agent file that runs one route's measurement and returns the numbers with its exit codes. Absent means verify-ui offers to install its own.

theme.description: Colour, tokens and the brand slot. Read by ingest-theme, record-design, add-primitive and paper.

dir.description: Folder holding the theme files. Null means the repo has one hardcoded look and ingest-theme writes a stylesheet instead.

registry.description: Source file listing every theme with its id and role. A theme absent from it is a theme no surface can pin.

contract.description: File declaring which tokens every theme owes. A gap is a token that silently inherits the enclosing surface.

generator.description: Command that emits a theme file from a source palette. Null means ingest-theme transcribes the supplied variables by hand.

doc.description: File stating the token contract, the theme roles and which modes a theme has.

components.description: The primitive layer and its catalogue. Read by add-primitive, new-screen, record-design and paper.

dir.description: Folder holding the primitives a screen composes. Checked before any interface is built, because the primitive usually exists.

install.description: Command that installs one primitive, with the component name appended. Null means a missing primitive is written by hand.

registry.description: Hand-maintained file listing the installed primitives a catalogue page renders. Null means the repo shows no catalogue, and add-primitive skips registration and says so.

showcase.description: Route where the catalogue renders, appended to dev.url to check an entry landed.

doc.description: File stating what a registry entry owes and which layer a component file belongs in.

surfaces.description: Where a screen goes and what its folder owes. Read by new-surface, new-screen, record-design, paper and receive-prototype.

root.description: Folder holding the surfaces, one per folder. Null means the repo has a single application and a screen goes wherever its route lives.

unit.description: What the repo calls one of them, in the words it uses. new-surface asks once where none is declared.

doc.description: File stating a surface folder's structure, its mandatory files and its import direction.

route.description: Url pattern one surface renders at, with the surface's folder name substituted for `<name>`.

compositionDoc.description: File holding the layout archetypes, the hierarchy rules and the four data states. Absent means new-screen uses its own bundled menu.

limits.description: Command that reports a file which has outgrown its size or component budget. Null means file shape is judged by reading.

seam.description: Folder holding the one path a surface's data goes through, which a real interface swaps for its own client. Null means data is fetched at the call site.

harnessMarkers.description: Strings that mark demo-only machinery, so a receiving developer can find every file to strip by grep rather than by memory.

receiveDoc.description: File stating what survives a handoff into a real application and what stays behind. Absent means receive-prototype uses its own bundled list.

check.description: One check: the command and the count it is allowed to return. Null means the repo has no check of this kind.

cmd.description: Shell command that runs the check. A typecheck command must build the project rather than only parse it — a parse-only flag is a false pass.

baseline.description: Count this check returns today and is allowed to keep returning. Anything above it is new.

cwd.description: Directory this check runs in, relative to the repo root. Overrides checks.cwd.
